Thunder Bay Hunt Map

Ten areas to scout for deer and grouse west and north of the city. All are on Crown land, use open logging roads, and sit within about 2 hours' drive.

    Before you go

    • No shooting from or across a road, and no loaded gun in or on any vehicle, ATV included.
    • Wear hunter orange during the deer gun season (Oct 10 to Dec 15).
    • Your deer licence comes with an antlered-only tag. To take a doe, you need an antlerless draw tag, an additional deer tag, or a party member who holds one.
    • Most provincial parks prohibit hunting. Conservation reserves generally allow it. First Nation reserves require permission.
    • The shaded "mostly private" areas are farms, homes and camps. Ask before you hunt there, even if it isn't posted.
    • No firearm discharge inside the City of Thunder Bay.
    • "Restricted" roads may be limited to forestry traffic. Read the signs at the road entrance.

    These areas are scouting starting points chosen from road, forest and fire data, not guaranteed hot spots. Confirm land status and rules on the ground. This map is not a legal survey.

    Data: Ontario MNRF via Land Information Ontario (forest roads, road barriers, Crown unpatented land, WMUs, parks, conservation reserves, First Nation reserves, fire history, waterbodies, Ontario Road Network), retrieved Oct 1, 2026, under the Open Government Licence – Ontario. Seasons from the 2026 Hunting Regulations Summary. Drive times are estimates from posted road types. Check land status in the Crown Land Use Policy Atlas.
